chunks: What Saʿd narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wearing silk and dībāj,

So he said: As for in warfare, there is no harm, even if it contains images. And it is possible that what is meant by dībāj is that which is mixed with cotton and linen, because salat (prayer) in that is permissible, and its being called dībāj would be by way of figurative usage; that indicates this.

key_terms.الدِّيبَاجِ: brocade or silk fabric, possibly referring here to a mixed textile
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity in such garments is under discussion
key_terms.الْحَرِيرِ: silk, especially as a material relevant to rulings of dress
key_terms.الْحَرْبِ: warfare, the circumstance in which the ruling is relaxed
key_terms.تَمَاثِيلُ: images or figures present on the garment
key_terms.لِبَاسِ: garment or clothing being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.مَخْلُوطًا: mixed, referring to fabric blended with other materials

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear silk or dībāj in warfare or pray in garments mixed with silk?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on silk and dībāj garments, stating that there is no harm in wearing them in warfare, even if they contain images. It also notes the possibility that dībāj here refers to fabric mixed with cotton and linen, in which salat (prayer) is permissible, indicating a juristic distinction regarding pure and mixed materials.
